scope: Different-author, static-only hammer review of the exact M1896 two-axis C2 hold-repair runner. The review rechecked the frozen M1811 DDC/SDC pairs, the sealed M1830 result, the corrected and sealed M1893R2 source authority, the exact M1892 Tcl, axis/area/timing policy, execution cardinality, freshness/resource checks, failure isolation, publication semantics and claim boundary. It performed no license query, attempt creation, Design Compiler, PrimeTime, Formality, VCS, PTPX, result publication, source mutation, predecessor mutation, or docs/359 mutation.
verdict: FAIL CLOSED. The exact M1896 source correctly binds the two M1811 input pairs and 5 percent per-axis area ceilings, carries one DC call site inside the exact two-axis loop, restores the 0.050 ns hold uncertainty after optimization at 0.070 ns, requires DC setup and hold MET, and preserves a raw logic-only/no-PT/no-Formality/no-power claim boundary. Launch is nevertheless forbidden because the authority is caller-self-pinned without the independently sealed release required by M1893R2; lmutil is queried before the attempt is consumed; the attempt can remain partial and unsealed on failures before WORK_ACTIVE is armed; mandatory design-rule closure is not gated; and no-replace publication has no post-move existence/seal proof and can silently no-op. No M1896 attempt, license query or EDA is authorized from this review.

findings.finding: The launch authority is self-pinned by caller-controlled environment variables and there is no independently sealed release.
findings.evidence: Lines 88-99 accept M1893R2 review SHA, M1897 review SHA and the runner SHA entirely from M1896_EXPECTED_* variables. The status and runner binding are substring greps. A replaced and freshly resealed M1893R2/M1897 pair plus a modified runner can therefore be supplied with mutually matching caller pins. M1893R2 explicitly requires an independently sealed release before EDA, but M1896 consumes none.
findings.impact: Review/runner separation is not fail-closed, so the exact reviewed source is not launch-authoritative.
findings.required_fix: Add a separately authored and double-sealed release whose exact SHA is pinned outside the runner invocation and whose schema, PASS status, zero P0/P1/P2, different reviewer, runner SHA, Tcl SHA, M1893R2 triplet, M1830 triplet and all frozen input pins are parsed semantically. Recheck it immediately before attempt consumption.

findings.finding: The license server is queried before the attempt is consumed.
findings.evidence: The lmutil call is line 130; LOCK/ATTEMPT/WORK creation begins at line 131. A failed or repeated lmutil query leaves no consumed attempt and the namespace remains launchable.
findings.impact: The one-shot budget does not cover the first external tool access and permits repeated pre-attempt license probes, directly violating the M1893R2 launch requirement.
findings.required_fix: Atomically create and seal the attempt before lmutil or any external EDA/license command. Any subsequent license failure must seal a no-retry quarantine.

findings.finding: Attempt creation is not failure-atomic and the failure trap is armed too late.
findings.evidence: One mkdir creates LOCK, ATTEMPT and WORK, then writes and seals ATTEMPT; WORK_ACTIVE becomes 1 only at line 134. Failure during mkdir after a partial create, ATTEMPT_CONSUMED.txt write or attempt sealing runs on_exit with WORK_ACTIVE=0, so neither partial ATTEMPT nor WORK is quarantined or sealed.
findings.impact: A consumed or partially consumed launch can be left without auditable terminal evidence, defeating the required partial-attempt fail-closed chain.
findings.required_fix: Arm a launch-state trap before namespace mutation, create the attempt in a temporary directory, seal and no-replace publish it atomically, then ensure every nonzero exit after any namespace write seals all surviving state into a terminal quarantine.

findings.finding: The mandatory design-rule closure gate from M1893R2 is absent.
findings.evidence: The M1892 Tcl emits reports/constraint_design_rules_posthold.rpt, but lines 158-177 neither require that file nor parse zero max-capacitance, max-transition, max-fanout, min-pulse-width and min-period violations. M1893R2 mandatory_future_result_gates requires drc_violations_max=0.
findings.impact: M1896 can publish RAW_PASS with setup and hold MET while design-rule violations remain, contrary to its upstream authority.
findings.required_fix: Emit a machine-readable posthold design-rule summary from the frozen Tcl and require status=MET and violating_paths=0 for both axes before publication.

findings.finding: Canonical no-replace publication has no post-move proof and can report success after a silent no-op.
findings.evidence: Line 191 uses mv -T -n. GNU mv -n may return success without moving when RESULT appears after the freshness check. Lines 192-195 immediately clear WORK_ACTIVE, disable traps, remove the lock and print success without checking that RESULT exists, WORK is absent, RESULT is not a symlink, or both result seals still verify.
findings.impact: A publication race can leave the reviewed work unpublished while the runner emits a success token and discards failure handling.
findings.required_fix: Use a publication primitive that fails if RESULT exists, then require RESULT regular-directory identity, WORK absence and full recursive seal verification before clearing WORK_ACTIVE or printing success.
